description: Eenmanszaak clients of Kees de Boekhouder who pay the fixed fee of EUR 840 per year ex VAT, invoiced monthly, for a personal, internally trained bookkeeper plus the client web and mobile app: the core of the more than 10,000 entrepreneurs the company serves from Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht, drawn from the roughly 1.2 million zzp'ers counted by CBS in 2025. The group spans the creative freelancer with many small receipts and an association behind them (BNO, DuPho, Kunstenbond, Stichting BOK), the higher-earning knowledge freelancer who compares Kees rationally with software-only tools and cares about deductions and the Wet DBA, and the starter who registers at the KVK for the first time, often next to a job. They share one job: administration that takes almost no time, quarterly VAT and the income tax return filed on time by a bookkeeper who carries the fiscal responsibility, and no surprise tax bill.

customers.name: Creative Freelancer
customers.description: A designer, photographer, stylist, make-up artist, furniture maker, illustrator, artist or content creator who runs an eenmanszaak and is the heart of the Kees de Boekhouder client base: the client stories of Jochem (furniture designer and maker), Celeste (stylist and influencer), Tynke (make-up artist and hairstylist) and Marloes (artist) all belong here. Typically a member of BNO, DuPho, Kunstenbond or Stichting BOK, earning an irregular income from a mix of assignments, commissions, day rates, licence fees and occasional grants, with many small purchases: materials, props, camera gear, studio rent, travel and subscriptions. Pays the fixed eenmanszaak fee of EUR 840 per year ex VAT, invoiced monthly, and often connects a business account through Ponto for EUR 5 per month. Wants administration to take almost no time, a bookkeeper who understands creative work (mixed private and business use, second-hand equipment, foreign clients, reverse-charge VAT for EU agencies) and the certainty that the quarterly VAT return and the income tax return are filed on time without a surprise bill. Judges the service on hours spent per month, on never missing a deadline and on a human being answering by e-mail or phone.

jobsToBeDone.name: Keep my administration complete with almost no time spent
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Keep every receipt, purchase invoice, sales invoice and bank transaction of the business captured, categorised and reviewed by a bookkeeper, without turning evenings and weekends into administration time. The job is to make the administration a by-product of running the creative business: a photo at the till, an invoice from the app, a bank connection that does the rest, and a bookkeeper who reviews and asks only when something is unclear.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: All bookings of a quarter are in the administration before the bookkeeper's review, with less than two hours of the freelancer's own time per month, no missing receipts at the VAT deadline and no backlog of unmatched bank transactions at year-end.

steps.step: Start with the bookkeeper and get the app set up
steps.description: After the free intro call, choose the eenmanszaak subscription, get access to mijn.keesdeboekhouder.nl and the mobile app, add the trading names clients know, and connect the business bank account through Ponto. Decide during the first upload coaching what counts as business (studio rent, camera, props) and what stays private, so later receipts need no discussion.

streamsNeeded.name: Start And Onboard A New Client
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the free Google Meet intro, the mutual-fit check, account access, bookkeeper assignment and the first upload coaching that sets the rules for what to capture.

streamsNeeded.name: Sync And Match Bank Transactions
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Establishes the Ponto PSD2 consent for the business account so that transactions arrive automatically from the first month.

steps.step: Capture every receipt the moment it happens
steps.description: Photograph the receipt at the art-supply store or the camera shop, forward the e-mail invoice from the stock-photo or software subscription, and let Scan & Herken recognise supplier, amount, VAT and category. Decide only on the exceptions the app flags: mixed private and business use, a second-hand purchase without VAT, a purchase from an EU webshop with reverse-charge VAT.

streamsNeeded.name: Capture Receipts And Expenses
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns a photo, upload or e-mail into a recognised, categorised expense booking with VAT, ready for the bookkeeper's review, so the freelancer does not type anything.

steps.step: Invoice from the app so revenue is booked automatically
steps.description: Create quotes and invoices in the app under the right trading name, with the correct VAT rule for a Dutch agency, an EU client (reverse charge) or a private customer, so that every sale is already in the administration and the bookkeeper never has to reconstruct revenue from bank statements.

streamsNeeded.name: Create Quotes And Invoices And Get Paid
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Produces the invoice as a booking with the right VAT treatment and tracks its status, so revenue is complete without extra work.

steps.step: Let the bank connection match the rest
steps.description: Check the app once a week: transactions synced four times a day are matched automatically against invoices and receipts; the freelancer confirms the few open ones, books a direct expense for a small purchase without a receipt, and re-authorises the bank consent when the app asks every 90 to 180 days. Friction: an expired consent silently stops the sync and creates a backlog.

streamsNeeded.name: Sync And Match Bank Transactions
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Syncs and auto-matches transactions and asks for manual matching or direct booking only for the remainder; flags consent expiry before the sync stops.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Your Finances On The Dashboard
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows the open to-dos and unmatched transactions on web and mobile so the weekly check takes minutes.

steps.step: Respond to the bookkeeper's review questions
steps.description: Before each quarterly VAT return the bookkeeper checks the administration and asks about anything unclear: a large purchase that may be an investment, a receipt without VAT, a payment from a foreign platform. Answer by e-mail or phone, upload the missing document, and let the bookkeeper close the quarter.

streamsNeeded.name: Review Administration And File Vat Returns
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Structures the bookkeeper's check into concrete questions and to-dos for the client, so the quarter can be closed without a back-and-forth over e-mail.

streamsNeeded.name: Ask Your Bookkeeper And Get Advice
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Carries the questions and answers between client and bookkeeper by e-mail and phone, linked to the client file.

jobsToBeDone.name: Never miss a VAT or income tax deadline or get a surprise bill
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Have the quarterly btw-aangifte and the yearly income tax return prepared, checked and filed with the Belastingdienst before the deadline by a bookkeeper who carries the fiscal responsibility, and know throughout the year what to reserve for VAT and income tax so that an assessment never comes as a shock. The job is peace of mind: deadlines are someone else's calendar, deductions are applied, and the reserved amount matches the bill.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every VAT return is filed before the last day of the month after the quarter and every income tax return before its deadline, with zelfstandigenaftrek, mkb-winstvrijstelling and investment deductions applied, and the difference between the reserved amount and the final assessment stays within a small margin.

steps.step: Know the deadlines and what the bookkeeper needs
steps.description: Receive reminders in the app and by e-mail before the end of each quarter listing what is still missing (receipts, unmatched transactions, an invoice not yet sent), so the review can start on time. Friction: a reminder that arrives during a shoot week or a festival is easy to ignore.

streamsNeeded.name: Review Administration And File Vat Returns
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Sets the review cut-off per quarter and derives the client to-do list of missing bookings from the administration.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Your Finances On The Dashboard
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Surfaces deadlines, to-dos and notifications on the dashboard and in the mobile app.

steps.step: Have the quarter checked and the VAT return filed
steps.description: The bookkeeper reviews the bookings, corrects VAT categories where needed, confirms the VAT to pay or receive with the client and files the return through the official Belastingdienst channel; the client receives the amount and the payment reference with time to pay.

streamsNeeded.name: Review Administration And File Vat Returns
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the bookkeeper check, prepares the VAT return and files it with the Belastingdienst before the deadline, with the filed copy stored for the client.

steps.step: Reserve the right amount for income tax during the year
steps.description: Look at the dashboard's profit and tax reservation after each quarter and set money aside, or ask the bookkeeper to request a preliminary assessment (voorlopige aanslag) so that tax is paid monthly instead of in one lump. Decide with the bookkeeper whether an exceptionally good year justifies an investment before year-end.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Your Finances On The Dashboard
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows profit to date and the amount to reserve for VAT and income tax in real time as bookings are submitted.

streamsNeeded.name: Ask Your Bookkeeper And Get Advice
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Answers reservation questions and arranges a preliminary assessment so the tax bill is spread over the year.

steps.step: Close the year and file the income tax return
steps.description: Confirm the hours worked for the hours criterion, private use of the car or studio, and any investments; the bookkeeper prepares the annual figures, applies zelfstandigenaftrek (EUR 1,200 in 2026, EUR 900 in 2027), mkb-winstvrijstelling and investment deductions, and files the income tax return, plus a fiscal partner's return for EUR 125 incl. VAT when asked.

streamsNeeded.name: Close The Year And File Income Tax
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns the checked administration into annual accounts and a filed income tax return with the deductions applied, including the partner return add-on.

steps.step: Understand the assessment and deal with changes
steps.description: When the assessment arrives, compare it with what was reserved and ask the bookkeeper about any difference; receive proactive updates about rule changes that matter to creative freelancers, such as the shrinking zelfstandigenaftrek, the KOR threshold of EUR 20,000 and Wet DBA enforcement since 2025.

streamsNeeded.name: Ask Your Bookkeeper And Get Advice
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Explains the assessment and pushes proactive updates about deadlines and rule changes to the client, backed by the advice knowledge base.

jobsToBeDone.name: Get paid faster with professional quotes and invoices
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Send quotes and invoices that look professional under the trading name the client knows, apply the right VAT rule for agencies, EU clients and private customers, see which invoices are open and remind clients politely, so that cash arrives sooner and the freelancer spends less time chasing money. The job is to make invoicing part of the creative workflow rather than a separate chore in Word or Excel.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Invoices go out the day the work is delivered, the share of invoices paid within the payment term rises, overdue invoices are reminded automatically before the freelancer has to make an awkward call, and every invoice is already booked for VAT and revenue.

steps.step: Turn a request into a quote

streamsNeeded.name: Create Quotes And Invoices And Get Paid
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides quote templates per trading name with status tracking and one-click conversion to an invoice.

steps.step: Invoice with the right VAT rule
steps.description: Convert the accepted quote into an invoice, applying 21 percent VAT for a Dutch client, reverse charge for an EU agency, or the KOR exemption when the freelancer opted in, and attach it to the client's contact so the history is in one place.

streamsNeeded.name: Create Quotes And Invoices And Get Paid
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies VAT rules including reverse charge, keeps multiple trading names per entity and books the invoice as revenue.

streamsNeeded.name: Ask Your Bookkeeper And Get Advice
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Answers the occasional question about a foreign client or a licence fee before the invoice goes out.

steps.step: See what is open and when it was paid
steps.description: Watch the invoice status change to paid when the bank connection matches the incoming payment, and see days outstanding per client on the dashboard, without checking the bank app manually.

streamsNeeded.name: Sync And Match Bank Transactions
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Matches incoming payments to open invoices automatically so status is current without manual work.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Your Finances On The Dashboard
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows outstanding invoices and revenue per quarter in real time.

steps.step: Remind late payers without damaging the relationship
steps.description: Let the app send a friendly reminder after the payment term and a firmer one later, decide personally when to call, and ask the bookkeeper about statutory interest or a collection step for a client that never pays.

streamsNeeded.name: Create Quotes And Invoices And Get Paid
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Tracks overdue invoices and sends reminders in the freelancer's tone, with the option to escalate.

customerJourneyStories.name: From a shoebox of receipts to a bookkeeper on the phone
customerJourneyStories.summary: A furniture designer and maker in Amsterdam, three years into his eenmanszaak, moves from a shoebox of receipts and a once-a-year accountant to Kees de Boekhouder, from the fine that triggered the search to the second year in which he recommends Kees to his studio neighbours.

stages.narrative: A letter from the Belastingdienst announces a fine for a VAT return filed late, and the accountant who does the annual return replies that quarterly VAT was never part of the deal. The designer realises he has paid VAT he could have reclaimed on materials and that a good year of commissions has left nothing reserved for income tax.

A studio neighbour, a photographer and DuPho member, mentions that her bookkeeper at Kees de Boekhouder answers within a day and that DuPho members get a benefit. The designer reads the client story of Jochem, a fellow furniture maker, on keesdeboekhouder.nl and sees that a personal bookkeeper plus app costs EUR 840 per year, invoiced monthly.

He compares Kees with Moneybird and e-Boekhouden.nl, which are cheaper per month but leave the VAT and income tax filing to him, and with a local accountant who charges per hour. The free Google Meet intro settles it: the bookkeeper explains how mixed private and business use of the van and workshop is handled, confirms the first-year commitment and monthly cancellation afterwards, and that the fee includes the income tax return.

In the first two weeks he uploads the shoebox in batches with Scan & Herken, connects his Knab account through Ponto and lets the bookkeeper coach him through the first upload. The first quarter is reviewed with a handful of questions about a second-hand lathe and a purchase from a German supplier, and the VAT return is filed a week before the deadline.

Photographing receipts at the timber yard becomes a habit, invoices go out from the app under his studio name, and the dashboard shows what to reserve each quarter. When a gallery in Belgium commissions a piece he e-mails his bookkeeper about reverse-charge VAT and gets an answer the same afternoon.

After the first income tax return, with zelfstandigenaftrek and an investment deduction applied and an assessment close to what the dashboard had predicted, he stays without thinking about the alternatives. He records a client story for the Kees network profiles and two neighbours from the studio building book an intro call on his recommendation.

customerJourneyStories.name: From a first big year as a stylist to admin that fits in a phone
customerJourneyStories.summary: A stylist and content creator whose business grew from side gigs to a full-time eenmanszaak with brand deals and agency work adopts Kees de Boekhouder through a Kunstenbond member benefit, and stays because the app fits a life lived on set and on the road.

stages.narrative: A brand deal from an agency in Paris, a growing number of small purchases for shoots and a first income tax assessment that surprises her make it clear that a spreadsheet and a friend who 'knows tax' are no longer enough. She has no time in the evenings and no interest in learning bookkeeping.

A Kunstenbond newsletter lists Kees de Boekhouder as a member benefit, and a post by Celeste, a stylist and influencer, describes doing her whole administration from her phone with a bookkeeper who calls her back. The Kees website shows quotes and invoices, Scan & Herken and the dashboard on a mobile screen.

She checks that the app has a real iOS app, that foreign agency invoices are handled, that reminders for late payers can be sent in her own tone, and that the price is fixed at EUR 70 per month with a bank connection for EUR 5 extra. The intro call confirms that a bookkeeper who has other creative clients will be assigned and that there is no charge for questions.

She signs up, connects her bunq account, photographs the receipts of her first shoot week and sends three invoices from the app, one with reverse-charge VAT to the Paris agency. The bookkeeper reviews the first month, corrects two categories and explains which part of her clothing budget can be business.

The app becomes part of set life: a receipt is photographed before the coffee is cold, brand deals are invoiced the day the content is delivered, and overdue invoices are reminded automatically. Each quarter the VAT amount and payment reference arrive by e-mail before the deadline, and the dashboard tells her what to reserve.

After a year her days sales outstanding have dropped and the income tax return holds no surprises. When a software-only tool offers a cheaper plan she stays, because the bookkeeper knows her business and has already flagged the Wet DBA questions on a long-term agency contract. She joins the Kees entrepreneur network and refers two fellow creators.

customers.name: Knowledge Freelancer
customers.description: A consultant, software developer, interim manager, project lead, coach or trainer who runs an eenmanszaak with a few larger clients at a time, invoices by the hour or per fixed-fee assignment and earns a higher revenue than the average zzp'er: often EUR 80,000 to 150,000 per year with relatively few, larger cost items such as a laptop, travel, training, pension contributions and a home office. Pays the fixed eenmanszaak fee of EUR 840 per year ex VAT, invoiced monthly, usually with a bank connection through Ponto at EUR 5 per month, and frequently adds the partner income tax return for EUR 125 incl. VAT. Sensitive to the Wet DBA (enforced by the Belastingdienst since 1 January 2025 with a soft landing in 2026), to claiming every deduction (zelfstandigenaftrek of EUR 1,200 in 2026, mkb-winstvrijstelling, pension and investment deductions) and to knowing the real profit and the tax to reserve at any moment. Faces big decisions along the way: buying a house on a freelancer's income, moving to a BV once profit stays high, choosing a pension product. Compares Kees de Boekhouder rationally with software-only tools such as Moneybird, Jortt or Tellow and with an accountant who charges per hour, and chooses the personal bookkeeper for the accuracy and the advice, not for the app alone.

jobsToBeDone.outcome: The dashboard shows profit, VAT position and tax reservation that stay within a small margin of what the bookkeeper files and the Belastingdienst assesses, so that reservations, investments and a mortgage application can be based on the numbers on screen.

steps.step: Connect the bank and keep transactions matched

streamsNeeded.name: Create Quotes And Invoices And Get Paid

steps.step: Book the few larger costs and investments correctly

streamsNeeded.name: Ask Your Bookkeeper And Get Advice

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Your Finances On The Dashboard

jobsToBeDone.name: Claim every deduction and stay on the right side of the Wet DBA
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Make sure that the income tax return uses every deduction the freelancer is entitled to, that the evidence for the hours criterion and business use exists when the Belastingdienst asks, and that assignments are structured and documented so they do not look like sham self-employment under the Wet DBA. The job is to minimise tax legally and to keep the freelance status defensible.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The filed income tax return includes zelfstandigenaftrek, mkb-winstvrijstelling, pension, home office and investment deductions where applicable with evidence on file, and every long assignment has been checked against the Wet DBA indicators before it starts, with no reclassification or correction afterwards.

customerJourneyStories.name: From a self-service tool to a bookkeeper who reads the contract
customerJourneyStories.summary: A freelance software developer in Utrecht with one long assignment at a scale-up and a spreadsheet-plus-software-tool setup moves to Kees de Boekhouder after the Wet DBA enforcement makes his client nervous, and stays because the tax position on the dashboard finally matches the assessment.

stages.narrative: In early 2025 his client's legal team asks every freelancer to confirm that their contract survives the Belastingdienst's Wet DBA enforcement. The developer realises his software tool files returns but gives no advice, and that his last income tax return missed the pension deduction he thought he had claimed.

A fellow developer in a Slack community mentions that his bookkeeper at Kees de Boekhouder checked his contract and rewrote two clauses. The Kees website lists a fixed price of EUR 840 per year with a personal bookkeeper, an FAQ about the Wet DBA and a free intro call via Google Meet.

He builds a comparison: Moneybird and Jortt cost less per month but leave him with the filing and no adviser, Tellow's plan with a bookkeeper is close in price, and an accountant quotes hourly rates for advice. The intro call is decisive: the bookkeeper explains the Wet DBA indicators, the hours criterion evidence and how the dashboard shows the income tax reservation, and confirms that questions are included in the fee.

He switches mid-year: Kees imports digital copies of the previous returns, he connects his Rabobank account via Ponto and sends his monthly invoice from the app. The bookkeeper reviews the contract, advises a change in the exclusivity clause and requests a preliminary assessment so income tax is paid monthly.

The monthly routine takes fifteen minutes: invoice, confirm two bank matches, upload a training invoice. Each quarter the bookkeeper confirms the VAT position and the dashboard's reservation; the year-end return includes zelfstandigenaftrek, mkb-winstvrijstelling and the pension contribution, with his partner's return added for EUR 125.

When his profit stays above the level where a BV starts to make sense, the bookkeeper runs the comparison and Founders takes over the BV setup without a change of platform. He renews without looking at alternatives and points two colleagues from the scale-up to the intro call.

customerJourneyStories.name: From an hourly accountant to mortgage-ready figures at a fixed fee
customerJourneyStories.summary: An interim project manager in Rotterdam, tired of her accountant's hourly invoices for every question, adopts Kees de Boekhouder while preparing to buy a house on freelance income, and stays for the predictable cost and the advice that comes with it.

stages.narrative: A mortgage adviser asks for three years of annual figures and a current-year forecast within two weeks, and her accountant quotes a separate fee and a three-week lead time. Her last invoice from the accountant included charges for two e-mails about a preliminary assessment.

A search for 'boekhouder zzp hypotheek' and a recommendation from a former colleague lead her to Kees de Boekhouder's blog on buying a house as a freelancer and the Rotterdam office at Stationsplein. She books the free Google Meet intro the same day.

She checks whether the fixed fee really includes advice and the income tax return, whether her previous returns can be transferred, how quickly the annual figures can be ready, and what the first-year commitment and monthly cancellation afterwards mean. Client stories and the AVG-compliant processing agreement close the trust gap.

The switch service imports her previous returns and the bookkeeper produces the annual figures and forecast the mortgage lender accepts within the deadline. She connects her ABN AMRO account, starts invoicing from the app and the first quarter is reviewed with two questions about travel costs.

With the house bought, the dashboard becomes her monthly check on profit and the tax to reserve. She asks about a pension product and the BrightPensioen partner benefit, has her fiscal partner's return added, and receives an update from her bookkeeper when the zelfstandigenaftrek changes for 2027.

At the end of the first fiscal year the total cost is exactly what the website said, the assessment matches the reservation, and every question was answered without an invoice. She stays, recommends Kees in her interim managers' network and considers the VOF package when she starts a joint venture with a colleague.

customers.name: Starting Entrepreneur
customers.description: Someone who registers an eenmanszaak at the KVK for the first time, often next to a job or a study: a designer taking first paid assignments, a nurse or teacher starting to freelance a few days a week, a developer with a first client, a coach or a webshop owner. Has never filed a VAT return, does not know whether to opt into the KOR (VAT exemption up to EUR 20,000 turnover, relaxed since 1 January 2025), which costs count, what the 1,225-hour criterion means or that startersaftrek (EUR 2,123) comes on top of zelfstandigenaftrek (EUR 1,200 in 2026). Chooses the Starters package at the eenmanszaak fee of EUR 840 per year ex VAT, invoiced monthly, and wants the first quarter and the first income tax return done right rather than cheap: an over-eager software tool with a free first year is tempting, but the real risk is a wrong VAT number set-up, a missed first return or a private bank account full of mixed transactions. Represents the entry point of the funnel from the roughly 1.2 million zzp'ers counted by CBS in 2025: a client who starts small and becomes a creative or knowledge freelancer, a VOF partner or, later, a BV director on the same platform. Judges the service on how fast the set-up is complete, whether the first filings are right first time and how much of the starter deductions end up in the return.

The first quarterly VAT return and the first income tax return filed correctly and on time, without learning tax law first

Claiming startersaftrek (EUR 2,123) and zelfstandigenaftrek (EUR 1,200 in 2026) when the hours criterion is met, and understanding how the business interacts with a job
A fixed price of EUR 840 per year invoiced monthly, so the cost is known before the first revenue arrives
A human to ask stupid questions to, by e-mail or phone, without feeling judged or paying per question

A Starters package at the same fixed eenmanszaak fee, invoiced monthly, with the income tax return included

Starter content and 'Keep up' updates on entrepreneurship next to a job, the hours criterion and buying a house as a freelancer, written by the bookkeepers
A platform that grows with the business, from starter to VOF to BV through Founders, so the first bookkeeper can stay the bookkeeper

jobsToBeDone.name: Start my business with the administration set up right from day one
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Go from a KVK registration to a working administration in the first weeks: VAT number, the KOR decision, a business bank account connected, trading names, invoice templates and the rules for what is business and what is private, with a bookkeeper assigned who will carry the first filings. The job is to avoid the mistakes that cost hours and money to repair later.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Within two weeks of the intro call the starter has an active account, a connected business bank account, a recorded KOR decision, the first invoice sent from the app and the first receipts booked, and the bookkeeper has confirmed the set-up is complete for the first quarter.

jobsToBeDone.name: Learn what I can deduct and what I must reserve as a starter
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Understand, in plain language and with the starter's own numbers, which costs are deductible, how startersaftrek, zelfstandigenaftrek and mkb-winstvrijstelling work, what the hours criterion requires next to a job, and how much of every invoice to set aside for VAT and income tax. The job is financial literacy for the first years, delivered by the bookkeeper and the app rather than by a course.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The starter can explain what to reserve from an invoice and which costs count, keeps hours evidence from the first month, and the first two income tax returns include every starter deduction the starter is entitled to, with no reservation shortfall.

customerJourneyStories.name: From a KVK registration next to a job to a first year done right
customerJourneyStories.summary: A physiotherapist in Utrecht who starts freelancing two days a week next to her employed job registers at the KVK, picks Kees de Boekhouder's Starters package after comparing it with a free-for-starters software tool, and stays after a first year in which every filing was right first time.

stages.narrative: After registering an eenmanszaak at the KVK she receives a letter from the Belastingdienst with a VAT number and a first quarterly return date, plus a promotional e-mail from a software tool offering fifteen months free. She has no idea whether the KOR applies to her or what to do with her private bank account.

A colleague who freelances mentions that a real person at Kees de Boekhouder does her VAT returns and answers questions, and the Kees blog on entrepreneurship next to a job comes up in her search. The site offers a free intro via Google Meet and a Starters package at EUR 70 per month.

She compares the free software tool with Kees: the tool is free but she would file herself and learn the rules; Kees costs EUR 840 per year, includes the income tax return and a bookkeeper who has seen a hundred starters. The intro call explains the KOR trade-off, the hours criterion next to a job and the first-year commitment, and she decides that the first year is the year to get it right.

In two weeks she opens a Knab business account and connects it, adds her trading name, sends her first invoice from the app and photographs the first receipts during the upload coaching. The bookkeeper reviews the first quarter, moves two private expenses out, and files the first VAT return a week early.

The app becomes a Friday habit: receipts, invoices, two bank matches to confirm, a look at the reservation on the dashboard. At year-end she sends her salary statement and hours overview, and the bookkeeper files an income tax return that combines job and business with startersaftrek applied.

The assessment matches the dashboard's reservation within a small margin. After the first fiscal year she keeps the subscription, drops to one job day when the practice grows, asks the bookkeeper about the hours criterion again, and refers a fellow physiotherapist who is about to register at the KVK.

customerJourneyStories.name: From a free tool and a fine to a bookkeeper who explains
customerJourneyStories.summary: A junior developer who started a webshop and freelance work on a free accounting plan misses his first VAT return, receives a fine, and switches to Kees de Boekhouder through a friend's referral, staying because the reservations, deductions and explanations turn the second year into a calm one.

stages.narrative: The first quarterly return date passes unnoticed while he sets up the webshop; a letter announces a fine and an estimated assessment. The free tool sent no reminder and its help pages could not tell him whether his equipment purchase was deductible under the KOR he had ticked at the KVK.

A friend who freelances shows him the Kees mobile app and mentions that her bookkeeper flagged a deadline before she noticed it. The Kees website's FAQ on switching, the client stories and the Rotterdam office address give him the sense of a real company rather than another app.

He weighs the extra cost against the fine he just paid and the deductions he probably missed, checks that switching mid-year is possible and that the previous quarter can be corrected, and asks in the intro call whether he can still leave the KOR. The bookkeeper's answers and the fixed monthly invoice convince him.

The switch service imports what exists, the bookkeeper corrects the missed return and files an objection to the estimated assessment, and he connects his bunq account. The first receipts are photographed and the dashboard shows what to reserve from the webshop sales.

He uses the reservation on the dashboard every month, keeps hours evidence, and asks before buying a camera whether it is deductible. Reminders reach him before each quarter and the first full income tax return with Kees applies zelfstandigenaftrek and startersaftrek.

When the webshop grows he asks about payroll for a part-time helper and about a VOF with a friend, and the same bookkeeper stays with him. He records a client story for the Kees network and tells the developer community that the fine cost more than a year of Kees.
